'''Leadway Technology Investments Holdings Limited''' formerly known as '''Advanced Card Systems Holdings Limited''' & '''HNA Technology Investments Holdings''' is a Cayman Islands-incorporated offshore holding company. Its subsidiary, '''Advanced Card Systems Limited''', was incorporated in [[British Hong Kong]] in 1995 by Denny Wong. In 2017, [[HNA Group]], via HNA EcoTech Group and HNA EcoTech Group's subsidiary, acquired Advanced Card Systems Holdings as part of a [[reverse IPO]].

ACS develops [[smart cards]], smart card readers and related products, and distributes them to over one hundred countries. It was ranked by Frost & Sullivan as one of the world's top 3 suppliers and [[Asia Pacific]]'s top supplier of PC-linked Smart Card Readers.<ref>
{{cite web
 |url=http://www.frost.com/prod/servlet/report-toc.pag?repid=N7B7-01-00-00-00
 |title=World Smart Card Readers and Chipsets Market
 |author=Frost & Sullivan
 |date=7 June 2010
 |accessdate=12 April 2011
 |publisher=frost.com
}}
</ref> In 2010, 2014, and 2015, it was listed among ''[[Forbes Asia]]''{{'}}s "Best Under a Billion",<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.acs.com.hk/en/press-release/2068/acs-holdings-ltd.-receives-award-as-one-of-forbes-asias-best-under-a-billion-2015/ | title=ACS Receives Award as One of Forbes Asia's Best Under a Billion 2015 | date=11 November 2015 }}</ref> a prestigious list of 200 top-performing companies with sales between US$5 million and US$1 billion, selected from publicly listed enterprises in Asia Pacific.<ref>

==History==

Advanced Card Systems Holdings was acquired by [[HNA Group]], via a subsidiary HNA EcoTech Group ({{zh|s=海航生态科技集团}}) in January 2017.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mpfinance.com/fin/daily2.php?node=1484331439774&issue=20170114|script-title=zh:海航再買殼 逾5億入主龍傑智能卡|date=14 January 2017|accessdate=12 July 2018|newspaper=Ming Pao|publisher=Media Chinese International|location=Hong Kong|language=zh-hk}}</ref> HNA Group owned more than a third of the share capital of HNA EcoTech Group.<ref name=HNATechInv2017AR/> Advanced Card Systems Holdings was renamed to '''HNA Technology Investments Holdings Limited''' in August 2017.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20170804004716-260410|script-title=zh:龍傑智能卡控股有限公司通過更名為海航科技投資控股有限公司|newspaper=中時電子報|agency=EQS Group|publisher=Want Want China Times Media Group|language=zh-tw|date=4 August 2017|accessdate=12 July 2018}}</ref>

{{expand section|date=July 2018}}

==Products and services==
ACS develops and supplies smart card reading and writing devices, smart cards, and other related products categorized into the following product lines:
* Smart card and card [[operating systems]]
* PC-linked smart card readers
* Mobile card readers
* [[Radio-frequency identification|Contactless]] readers
* Smart card readers with PIN-pad
* PC-linked readers with [[mass storage]]
* Dynamic Password Generators
* Smart card reader modules
* [[Software development kits]]

ACS products are certified and compliant with global and national industry standards. These standards include NFC Forum Certification; [[EMV]] Level 1 & 2; [[Visa payWave]]; [[MasterCard PayPass]]; American ExpressPay; Discover Zip; UnionPay QuickPass; [[Mondex]]; EMV CAP and VISA DPA; qPBOC and [[PBOC]] (the People's Bank of China); [[Network for Electronic Transfers|NETS]] (Singapore); [[CE marking|CE]]; UL/CSA; U.S. [[Federal Communications Commission]] (FCC); [[Voluntary Control Council for Interference by Information Technology Equipment|VCCI]] (Voluntary Control Council for Interference by Information Technology Equipment); [[Federal Information Processing Standard|FIPS]] (Federal Information Processing Standards); and [[Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals]] (REACH).<ref name=multiple>{{cite web|url=http://www.acs.com.hk/dloads/results/eng/1612_2012_interim_ra_e.pdf|title= INTERIM RESULTS ANNOUNCEMENT FOR THE SIX MONTHS ENDED 30 JUNE 2012|accessdate=12 November 2012 }}</ref>

ACS also offers product customization services to meet customer specifications. These include custom branding on ACS smart card and reader products.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acs.com.hk/index.php?pid=customization|title= ACS Product Customization|accessdate=12 April 2011 }}</ref>

ACS also provides end-to-end, smart card‒based services. ACS has already delivered automatic fare collection (AFC), retail, and micropayment services all over the world.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acs.com.hk/en/services/|title= ACS Solutions|accessdate=8 August 2015 }}</ref>

Furthermore, ACS conducts consultation and training sessions to help grow the smart card industry. In 2008, ACS offered an elective course on smart card technology in [[De La Salle University]] – [[Manila]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.prlog.org/10110597-acs-offers-elective-course-in-de-la-salle-university-manila.html|title= ACS offers elective course in De La Salle University-Manila|date=27 August 2008|accessdate=12 April 2011 }}</ref> In 2010, it conducted the first ever basic smart card training in the Philippines. It also conducted a two-day training on smart cards in the Information Technology Services Center (ITSC) of the [[Chinese University of Hong Kong]] (CUHK).<ref>

==Applications==
System integrators, [[software developer]]s and service houses worldwide use ACS smart card and card reader technologies, to create smart card-based applications for security systems in various sectors, including [[banking]], [[transportation]], [[Identity document|identification]], [[e-health]], [[e-government]], [[access control]] and [[e-commerce]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acs.com.hk/index.php?pid=typical-applications|title= ACS Typical Applications|accessdate=12 April 2011 }}</ref>

===Banking===
In 2009, ACS deployed 100,000 ACR38 Smart Card Readers for the implementation of an online home banking project in an [[East Asian]] country. The project involved ACS's cooperation with the country's local bank and telecommunication company, to integrate ACS smart card technologies into [[VoIP]]-enabled desktop phones that customers used to access [[online banking]] services at home.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.globalsmart.com/Supplied%20Smart%20Car |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005162313/http://www.globalsmart.com/Supplied%20Smart%20Car |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 October 2011 |title=ACS Supplied 100,000 ACR38 Smart Card Readers for Online Home Banking Project in East Asia |date=2 September 2009 |access-date=18 February 2010 |publisher=globalsmart.com }}</ref>

In 2009, ACS also received over 60,000 orders of ACR30 Smart Card Readers from Hong Kong banks. This banks were complying with the Hong Kong secure e-banking project, which entailed using the [[Hong Kong Identity Card]].<ref name="secureidnews2006">{{cite web|url=http://www.secureidnews.com/2006/02/08/hong-kong-banks-using-acs-smart-card-readers-for-two-factor-authentication|title= Hong Kong banks using ACS smart card readers for two-factor authentication|date=8 February 2006|accessdate=19 February 2010|publisher=secureidnews.com}}</ref> Following [[Hong Kong Monetary Authority]] (HKMA) guidelines that took effect in July 2005, these banks employed two-factor authentication tools, like e-Cert, for high-risk online banking transactions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.paymentsnews.com/2005/05/hong_kong_to_re.html|title=Hong Kong Monetary Authority To Require Two-Factor Authentication For Online Banking|date=30 May 2005|accessdate=22 February 2010|publisher=paymentsnews.com|archive-date=1 September 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090901122048/http://www.paymentsnews.com/2005/05/hong_kong_to_re.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The [[Bank of America]] (Asia), BOC Credit Card (International) Limited, [[Bank of China]] (Hong Kong), Chiyu Banking Corporation Limited, [[Nanyang Commercial Bank]], [[Bank of Communications]] (Hong Kong Branch), [[The Bank of East Asia]], [[CITIC Ka Wah Bank]] and [[Dah Sing Bank]] all used ACS's ACR30 to read smart ID cards embedded with Hong Kong Post e-Cert.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.prlog.org/10120294-acs-was-chosen-by-world-olympians-association-woa-to-secure-its-events-in-2008-beijing-olympic.html|title= ACS was chosen by World Olympians Association (WOA) to secure its events in 2008 Beijing Olympic|date=22 September 2008|accessdate=22 February 2010}}</ref>

===Access control===
In 2011, ACS was chosen as a smart card reader supplier for a service intended to secure US embassies worldwide. The [[US Department of State]] (DoS) had initiated a tender for a reader to secure physical and logical networks for embassy employees. Partnered with one of the bidders, ACS proposed the ACR3801 Smart card reader, a TAA-compliant, FIPS 201‒certified PC-linked reader. These standards enabled the ACR3801 to meet the security challenges presented by the DoS.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acs.com.hk/en/business-case/|title= Securing US Embassies Worldwide with the ACR3801 for US Department of State|accessdate=9 October 2015|publisher=acs.com.hk}}</ref>

ACS also participated in the security enhancement project set up by the [[World Olympians Association]] (WOA) for the [[2008 Beijing Olympics]]. ACS provided ACOS3 [[Microcontroller]] Smart Cards to identify around 4,000 guests, and ACR88 Handheld PIN-Pad Readers to read the smart cards.<ref name="secureidnews2006"/> ACS partnered with Artemis Solutions Group (ASG), which specialized in providing a complete credential management system for attendees of the Olympic Reunion Center (ORC).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.morerfid.com/details.php?subdetail=Report&action=details&report_id=6097 |title=Manage the new Singapore ez-link card at home with an ACR122 NFC Reader |date=18 August 2009 |access-date=22 February 2010 |publisher=morerfid.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928230454/http://www.morerfid.com/details.php?subdetail=Report&action=details&report_id=6097 |archive-date=28 September 2011 }}</ref>

===Transportation===
In August 2009, ACS supplied ACR122 [[Near Field Communication]] (NFC) Readers for [[EZ-Link]] cardholders to manage their new EZ-Link cards at home. Via the EZ-Online System, cardholders can check and print their 20 most recent transaction records, top-up their cards from a bank account, and load EZ-Coupons that may be used to redeem bonuses once the Ez-Link cards are presented to retail shops.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.micardreader.com/a358288-beijing-olympic-reunion-center-access-secured.cfm|title=Beijing Olympic Reunion Center Access Secured With BioCert Encrypted Smart Card Technology and Portable Identity Verification|date=27 August 2008|accessdate=18 February 2010|publisher=micardreader.com}}{{Dead link|date=January 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Government===
In 2013, ACS was chosen by a Middle Eastern country's Ministry of Labour to supply smart card readers that will help make labour transactions paperless and performable outside government offices. ACS supplied the ACR89, which was distributed directly to organizations and installed in service centers throughout the country, so that they may be more conveniently accessed by company operators and owners. This accessibility, coupled with a secure authentication system, generated savings for both the government, and various companies and organizations; simplified processes; and improved records management.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acs.com.hk/en/press-release/1160/acss-acr89-helps-streamline-labor-related-processes-in-middle-eastern-country/|title= ACS's ACR89 Helps Streamline Labor-Related Processes in Middle Eastern Country=13 September 2013|date = 19 September 2013|accessdate=8 April 2014|publisher=acs.com.hk}}</ref>

Also, over 100,000 ACS ACR38 Smart Card Readers were deployed during the pilot run of the project, "Belgian eID card reader for the 12-year-olds" in 2006. The decision to utilize ACS smart card readers was issued by the Federal Information and Communication Technology (FedICT) Department of the Belgian Government.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.secureidnews.com/2006/05/08/acs-smart-card-reader-chosen-for-belgian-id-card-project|title= ACS' smart card reader chosen for Belgian ID card project|date=8 May 2006|accessdate=19 February 2010|publisher=secureidnews.com}}</ref>

In the same year, the [[Egypt]]ian Government, began issuing smart [[taxation]] cards to taxpayers for security reasons. ACS's ACR100 SIMFlash Smart Card Readers were used to input, check and back-up transaction information of the taxpayers.<ref>
{{cite web
 |url=http://www.frost.com/prod/servlet/market-insight-top.pag?docid=92710322
 |title=Movers & Shakers Interview with Mr. Denny Wong, Chairman and CEO, Advanced Card Systems Ltd
 |author=Frost & Sullivan
 |date=17 January 2007
 |accessdate=19 February 2010
 |publisher=frost.com
}}
</ref>

===eHealth===
In 2008, ACS won a tender to supply 600,000 units of PC-linked contact smart card readers to the regional government of [[Lombardia]], [[Italy]]. The readers were used for read and write operations on health cards used by Lombardian citizens, pharmacies, doctors, hospitals, etc., to access medical services, as well as online government services.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.quamnet.com/companySearchDetail.action?coId=1226|title= Business Review – For the year ended December 31, 2008|date=31 December 2008|access-date=18 February 2010|publisher=quamnet.com| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100324071955/http://www.quamnet.com/companySearchDetail.action?coId=1226&| archive-date= 24 March 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>

===Retails===
In 2013, ACS was chosen as the primary technology partner of the Philippines' largest mall developer/operator and retail company for an end-to-end loyalty, payment, and automated fare collection (AFC) service. ACS's scalable service enabled faster and convenient transactions for mall visitors, while improving generation, accessibility, and management of transaction reports.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acs.com.hk/en/press-release/791/acs-solution-helps-increase-convenience-and-security-in-sm-prepaid-and-loyalty-program/|title= ACS Solution Helps Increase Convenience and Security in SM Prepaid and Loyalty Program|date=20 June 2013|accessdate=8 April 2014|publisher=acs.com.hk}}</ref>
 
In 2006, ACS's ACR120 contactless smart card readers were adopted by a high-end Japanese supermarket in Hong Kong for its customer [[loyalty program]], which began transitioning from contact to contactless smart card technology in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smartcardstrends.com/det_atc.php?idu=3840&main=e02340ad2dd44aaf2307cd95e5a8272e|title=ACS' Contactless Smart Card Reader is adopted by a high-end Japanese Supermarket for Loyalty Program|date=4 July 2006|accessdate=18 February 2010|publisher=smartcardstrends.com|archive-date=5 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005162243/http://www.smartcardstrends.com/det_atc.php?idu=3840&main=e02340ad2dd44aaf2307cd95e5a8272e|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

Meanwhile, ACS was selected to provide ACR122 contactless card readers to [[Pacific Century CyberWorks]] Limited (PCCW) Hong Kong in 2008. ACR 122 [[Octopus card]] readers were made available to be connected to PCCW's multimedia VoIP phone, thus allowing cardholders to check their card balance and their ten most recent transactions in the Hong Kong Octopus Card without the need for Octopus Enquiry Machines that are located in MTR stations only.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smartcardstrends.com/det_atc.php?idu=6761&main=e02340ad2dd44aaf2307cd95e5a8272e|title=Checking your Octopus card balance at home by ACR122 Octopus Card Reader|date=6 March 2008|accessdate=18 February 2010|publisher=smartcardstrends.com|archive-date=5 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005162257/http://www.smartcardstrends.com/det_atc.php?idu=6761&main=e02340ad2dd44aaf2307cd95e5a8272e|url-status=usurped}}</ref>
